title: Push Scores Without a Two-Way Channel
description: A browser scoreboard needs server-to-client text updates every few seconds. Clients send occasional commands with normal HTTP. Which simple push transport fits?

options.text: WebRTC with peer discovery and media relays.
options.explanation: Peer-to-peer media infrastructure adds complexity without serving this one-way server feed.

options.text: A new page load for every score.
options.explanation: Reloading adds unnecessary page and connection work and is not a continuous push channel.

options.text: Server-Sent Events with reconnect and a server-side replay path.
options.explanation: SSE fits one-way text updates over HTTP. Last-Event-ID can support catch-up, but the server must retain events to replay.

options.text: WebSockets because one-way text cannot use HTTP streaming.
options.explanation: HTTP streaming through SSE supports this directly; full duplex is useful when both sides send frequently.
